What you're paying for

No emergency premium

A 3am callout is billed at the same hourly rate as a Tuesday afternoon. No several-hundred-dollar surcharge for bad timing.

Reach him any hour

Phone, text or email, 24 hours a day. Not a call centre or a ticket queue — James directly.

Same-day response

Normal callouts often within hours. Emergencies, as soon as he can physically get there.

Someone who knows the property

The same licensed tradesman every time, who already knows where your shutoff valve is.

Seasonal walkthroughs

Gutters, exterior and weatherproofing checked ahead of the seasons that cause the damage — not after.

Rental turnover support

Repairs and touch-ups handled between tenants, on your schedule, for owners who aren't local.

What it costs

The retainer

$50 per month, per property. This covers 24-hour access, seasonal walkthroughs, and removes emergency callout fees. Landlords with several units pay per property.

The work itself

Billed at James's standard hourly rate, plus materials and any other costs incurred. The retainer isn't a labour plan — it's what makes sure someone answers, and that calling at midnight doesn't cost more than calling at noon.

Who it suits

Landlords and rental owners, people managing property from out of state, and homeowners who'd rather have one licensed number to call than start searching when something breaks.

The maths

A single after-hours emergency callout from a contractor typically carries a premium of several hundred dollars before anyone picks up a tool. At $50 a month, one 3am call in a year and the retainer has more than paid for itself — and most properties have more than one.

Register now

Why places are limited

Snow clearance runs on a fixed round, worked by one person with snowblowers. After a storm there are only so many hours before people need to get out of their driveways — which puts a hard limit on how many properties can be on the round and still be cleared properly.

That limit is the reason the register closes. Once the season starts, the properties on the list are the properties that get cleared; there's no adding a driveway mid-storm. Registering before 30 September is what secures a place for the winter.

What's covered

Snow clearance

Driveways, paths and access areas cleared with snowblowers, no matter the depth.

Deicing

Treatment to keep cleared surfaces safe once the snow is off them.

Residential & commercial

Both, on the same register. Commercial properties with early-morning access needs are worth flagging when you sign up.

Where it runs

Snow clearance covers a tighter area than James's other work — Newton, Lexington, Arlington, Belmont and Waltham only. A snowblower round has to stay compact to get everyone cleared in the hours after a storm.

Pricing

Charged per cubic foot, per snow event — so you pay for the snow that actually falls, not a flat fee for a winter that might be mild. James will confirm the rate for your property before the season starts.

Why snowblowers, not plows

Plows are quick, and they're also what scrapes up driveway surfaces, tears lawn edges and buries mailboxes. Every property on this register is cleared with snowblowers. It takes longer. Nothing underneath gets wrecked.

Who is Handyman James?

Frequently asked questions

Is Handyman James licensed and insured?

Yes. James holds an unrestricted Massachusetts Construction Supervisor License (CSL #120385) and is a registered Home Improvement Contractor (HIC #197410) — the state registration that gives clients access to the Guaranty Fund and arbitration program if something goes wrong. He also carries insurance. If a job falls outside his license, he'll say so before starting the work, not after.

What areas does Handyman James serve?

Newton, Lexington, Arlington, Waltham, Lincoln, Concord, Wellesley, Belmont, Cambridge, and Boston, Massachusetts. He's based in Newton. If you're just outside these areas, it's still worth asking.

What's the difference between a handyman and a general contractor?

A handyman typically handles smaller repairs and maintenance jobs, while a general contractor manages larger construction projects that require permits and specialty licensing. James holds an unrestricted Massachusetts Construction Supervisor License, which reflects that broader qualification, even though his day-to-day work is handyman and property management.

How much does the 24/7 on-call service cost?

$50 per month, per property. That covers 24-hour access by phone, text and email, and means there's no emergency callout premium — a 3am call is billed at the same hourly rate as a weekday afternoon. Labour is charged at the standard hourly rate plus materials. More about property management & on-call →

Is there emergency or 24/7 handyman service available?

Yes, for property management clients — both homeowners and rental property owners. James offers 24/7 on-call support alongside routine seasonal maintenance.

Which towns does snow clearance cover?

Snow clearance covers a smaller area than the rest of the work: Newton, Lexington, Arlington, Belmont and Waltham only. A snowblower round has to stay compact to get every property cleared in the hours after a storm. Handyman work and property management cover all ten towns.

How does snow removal work — do you use a plow?

No. James clears snow and ice using snow blowers only, for both residential and commercial properties. It's slower than plowing, but it avoids the driveway and lawn damage a plow can cause.

Is any job too small?

No. James takes on jobs many contractors won't bother with, from hanging a single picture to repairing old machinery. If it's a job that's outside his license or skills, he'll tell you upfront.

How much does a handyman cost in the Newton area?

It depends on the scope of the job. The most accurate way to get a number is to describe the work directly — contact James with details and he'll give you a straight answer.

How do I get a quote from Handyman James?

Call (508) 306-1552, email info@handyman-james.com, or send a message through the contact form. James responds personally, usually the same day.
